newsitem.title: GREECE: GRIGORIADIS BECOMES CHIEF MARKET ANALYST AT IFC.
newsitem.headline: GRIGORIADIS BECOMES CHIEF MARKET ANALYST AT IFC.

text.p: Constantinos Grigoriadis was promoted to chief market analyst for European Emerging Markets at the Washington-based International Finance Corporation's (IFC) Emerging Markets Group.

The IFC is one of the world's leading sources of information on stock markets in developing countries. A member of the World Bank Group, the IFC is the world's largest multilateral source of financing for private enterprises in emerging economies.

Grigoriadis is the architect of all IFC indexes in central and eastern Europe since May 1993, responsible for research and analysis of emerging markets in Russia, Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, Czech Republic, Bulgaria, Romania, Albania, Slovenia, Croatia and Yugoslavia.
He was responsible for Greece and Turkey from May 1993 to December 1994.
Using a sample of stocks in each market, the IFC calculates indexes of stock market performance designed to serve as benchmarks that are consistent across national boundaries.

"This eliminates inconsistencies that make it difficult to compare locally produced indexes computed with differing methodologies. IFC indexes are widely used by portfolio managers as they provide an objective and reliable benchmark," the IFC said.
IFC indexes are weighted by market capitalisation using a formula based on the chained Paasche method.

Price indexes are derived from changes in prices, adjusted for changes in capitalisation. IFC's total return indexes include changes from adjusted prices as well as cash dividends received and dividends implicit in rights issues with a subscription price below the prevailing market price.

"The price index is used to allow comparison of returns on a common basis across the index series. Although most markets have thair own locally calculated indexes, the methods used for computing them are different among markets and international investors cannot use themfor comparative purposes," the IFC said. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
